item.title: Simple exercise can be quite beneficial for Seniors
item.description: Missourians age 65 and older make up 17.5% of the state’s population, and that share is projected to exceed 20% by 2030, according to the Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services.Falls are a leading cause of injury among older adults and they are costly. The CDC estimates falls cost Missouri $883 million each year. item.title: Winter will return: Stay safe in cold weather
Your Stress Relief Toolkit for the New Year
item.description: Feeling stressed? These simple habits help you keep things under control.If reducing stress is one of your goals for the new year, congratulations on taking an important step in keeping yourself healthier. While a little stress is normal, dealing with too much for too long can take a toll. Chronic stress has been linked to headaches, poor sleep, weakened immunity and a higher risk of heart disease. item.title: Archie middle school Students of the Month
item.description: Congratulations to Archie Middle School and High School December Students of the Month, Charlie Snook and Ethan Robling! These students were selected for consistently demonstrating the character trait of compassion. Through their kindness, empathy, and willingness to support others, they have made a positive impact on their peers and our school. We are proud to recognize them for setting an example of caring and respect for those around them. Keep up the great work!

item.title: Drexel schools welcome new educator
item.description: Meet Mrs. Reagan Thomas, Title I Paraeducator and 2018 alumni of DrexelShe helps students in grades K-5 with math and reading, as well as, K-2 Library Specials. She guides kids with kindness, understanding, and an excellent sense of humor.She is currently attending Central Methodist University, majoring in Elementary Education and is married to Brandon Thomas (Drexel Alumni) with 2 children together.We are excited to have Mrs. Thomas as a Bobcat!

item.title: Ellett Memorial Hospital asks for your help
item.description: From the desk of EMH CEO, Laura SmithHow you can help us. Ellett Memorial Hospital and the Appleton City Rural Health Clinic aren't just places you go when you're sick - they're part of who we are as a community. The people who work here are your neighbors, friends, and sometimes even family. Our staff have deep roots in this town, and they care about you because they live here too. They show up every day with pride, compassion, and a genuine commitment to keeping high-quality care close to home
